login_help_text: We'll open the right space for you after you sign in.
login_admin_access: an admin will set up your access.
mfa_help_text: Open your authenticator app and enter the current 6-digit code, or use one of your single-use backup codes.
password_requirements: At least 12 characters. A passphrase of several unrelated words is strongest; common or breached passwords are refused.
profile_help: Your personal contact details. The email address stored here is the one that receives your password-reset link: without it, the self-service reset cannot reach you.
profile_email_hint: Used for password reset and email notifications.
profile_org_readonly: This information is managed by your administrator and cannot be edited here. Report any error to your manager or HR administrator.
profile_admin_readonly: The contact details of an administrator account are managed through administrator management and cannot be edited here.
sessions_help: These are the devices currently signed in to your account. If you don't recognise one, sign out all other sessions and change your password.
mfa_setup_step1: Scan this QR code with your authenticator app (Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator, Authy…):
mfa_setup_qr_alt: QR code for your authenticator app
mfa_setup_manual: Can't scan? Enter this key manually:
mfa_setup_step2: Enter the 6-digit code your app shows now:
mfa_setup_backup_note: After confirmation you'll receive single-use backup codes — store them somewhere safe.
mfa_manage_active_body: Your account is protected with an authenticator app. You will be asked for a 6-digit code at every sign-in.
mfa_manage_backup_left_note: Each backup code can be used once instead of an authenticator code.
mfa_manage_disable_label: To deactivate, confirm with a current authenticator code (or a backup code):
mfa_manage_inactive_body: Your account is protected by password only.
mfa_manage_privileged_warning: Your role is privileged — activating two-factor authentication is strongly recommended.
mfa_manage_explainer: Two-factor authentication adds a second step at sign-in: a 6-digit code from an authenticator app on your phone (Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator, Authy…). You'll also receive single-use backup codes in case you lose your phone.
mfa_backup_now_active: Two-factor authentication is now active on your account.
mfa_backup_store_note: Store these single-use backup codes somewhere safe (password manager, printed copy). Each works once instead of an authenticator code — for example if you lose your phone.
mfa_backup_shown_once: They are shown only this once.
sessmon_help: Every active session on the platform — who is signed in, from where, and since when. Close any session to force that device to sign in again. Sessions also expire on their own after inactivity.
sessmon_anonymous: {{n}} anonymous pre-login session(s) (login page, SSO handshake) are not listed.
sessmon_close_tooltip: Force-close this session (the device is signed out immediately)
sessmon_close_confirm: Close this session? The user on that device will be signed out immediately.

help_manual_intro: Follow these steps to set up and use the system effectively.
help_s1_login_d: Sign in with the administrator credentials provided to you (the installer sets a unique random password — never a default).
help_s1_pwd_d: Go to User Profile > Change Password immediately.
help_s2_dept_d: Add functional units (e.g. "IT", "HR") under the site.
help_s2_svc_d: Add specific teams (e.g. "DevOps") under the department.
help_s3_skill_d: Add specific skills to each domain (e.g. "JavaScript", "Communication").
help_s4_req_d: Select the skills and expected proficiency levels for each role.
help_s5_struct_d: Link them to a site / department / service.
help_s5_role_d: Give them a job role (which carries the required skills).
help_s6_sa_d: Employees rate their own skills (Dashboard or Self-Assessment page).
help_s6_val_d: Managers review and approve or adjust the ratings.
help_s6_ana_d: Open "Skill Matrix" or "Dashboard" to see gaps and readiness.

ga_intro: Skill gaps across your team, measured against each role's required levels. Turn a gap into action: open a profile to start coaching, a development plan or goals, or jump to the coaching console.
ga_legend: A gap is a required skill rated below its required level. Ready means every required skill is met. "Not measured" skills have no rating yet — they are never counted as zero.

notif_prefs_email_hint: When off, you still see everything in-app (bell) — no email.
notif_prefs_quiet_hint: Notifications during this window are held back.
notif_prefs_quiet_detail: During this window nothing appears in the bell and no email is sent — everything is delivered when the window ends. Set both times, or leave both empty to switch it off.
notif_prefs_quiet_invalid: Set a start time AND a different end time, or leave both empty.

help_emp_manual_intro: Everything you can do from your own space, in the order it comes up.
help_e1_login_d: open the "Set my password" link you received by e-mail (valid 72 hours), or use the temporary password your administrator handed you (or your company button if single sign-on is enabled).
help_e1_pwd_d: you are asked to change it on first sign-in. Pick one only you know.
help_e2_open_d: the page lists the skills expected for your role. The counter at the top says how many you have already rated.
help_e2_rate_d: pick the level that describes what you can do today, not what you are aiming for. A comment helps your manager understand your choice.
help_e2_submit_d: once submitted, your self-assessment goes for review. You can follow it in “My status”.
help_e3_status_d: where each skill stands — to do, under review, approved.
help_e3_reviews_d: your manager’s decision, and the button to dispute it if you disagree. A reason is required — that is what gets read.
help_e4_dev_d: your live plans (development, performance) and your objectives.
help_e4_learn_d: the courses assigned to you and how far along you are.
help_e4_cert_d: your certifications and when they expire — you are the one who books the revalidation.
help_e5_opp_d: internal openings; you can apply and attach a note.
help_e5_coach_d: your coaching sessions and actions, and the progress you record.
help_e5_help_d: the “?” button is on every page; the full guide is in the Help menu.

notif_prefs_site_quiet: Without quiet hours of your own, your site’s apply: from {{start}} to {{end}} (server time).
notif_prefs_grid_hint: Everything stays visible in the app. Untick a category to stop receiving it by e-mail.
notif_prefs_mandatory_note: “Mandatory” rows (workplace safety, account security) are always sent and cannot be switched off. Only an administrator stopping all e-mail suspends them.
notif_prefs_digest_hint: One e-mail that gathers what arrived for you.
notif_prefs_stepdown_note: Your last summaries were not opened: their frequency went from “{{from}}” to “{{to}}”.
notif_prefs_lang_hint: Each e-mail is written in a single language.
notif_prefs_ics_hint: Attaches an .ics file to e-mails that announce a deadline. It only holds the date and a generic label.
notif_shared_note: Shared computer: only the type of each notification is shown. Open it to see the details.
ncat_subtitle: {{n}} notification types: channels, recipients, mandatory or not, severity, subject and 30-day volume.
ncat_load_error: This page could not be loaded.
ncat_webhook_opt-in: Webhook: when a SuperAdmin allows it
ncat_volume_note: The volume counts the notifications created in the app over the last 30 days; “—” means it could not be read or the type exists by e-mail only.
ncat_site_hint: They apply to the people of the site who have not chosen quiet hours of their own. Sites have no time zone: the time is the server’s.
ncat_rcpt_team: The manager of the person concerned
ncat_rcpt_sa: The person assessed or their reviewer, depending on the step
ncat_rcpt_cycle: The campaign participants; their reviewers for escalations
ncat_rcpt_review: The reviewer or the person reviewed
ncat_rcpt_mc: The approver of the action, then its author
ncat_rcpt_dispute: The parties to the dispute and its arbiter
ncat_rcpt_coaching: The person, their manager and their coach
ncat_rcpt_lms: The person enrolled in the course
ncat_rcpt_safety: The person, their manager and the HSE lead
ncat_rcpt_oneonone: The other participant of the one-to-one
ncat_rcpt_digest: Each person, for what concerns them
ncat_rcpt_report: The owner of the scheduled report
nmet_subtitle: Per type, over the last {{days}} days, for the notifications sent since measuring began.
nmet_global_optout: People with no e-mail at all (all switched off)
nmet_stepdowns: Summaries slowed down for lack of opening
nmet_empty: No measurable notification over the period.
nmet_note_opened: “Opened”: the person followed the notification link, from the app or an e-mail. “Mark all as read” does not count; no tracking pixel is used.
nmet_note_acted: “Acted upon” is measured only for types whose action is recorded: self-assessment submitted, review decided, certificate recorded, successor named.
nmet_note_low: A type opened by fewer than 20% of its recipients is flagged; mandatory types never are.
nmet_note_scope: People who left, were voided or erased are excluded from every figure. No name appears on this page.
